column1: # Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored; a field containing a comma is double-quoted.
# A rule is **confronted** on a baseline when some observation of its collector carries the fields the
# rule's `match` names and comes within one unsatisfied condition of firing it — the baseline was asked
# the rule's question and answered no. A rule no baseline confronts is quiet there for a reason that
# says nothing about the rule
column2: so the gate's green is not evidence about it. ADR 0033 has the reasoning.

column1: # The gate reads this file strictly
column2: for the same reason `known-fps.csv` is read strictly:

column1: #   - `rule_id` must be a rule in the bundle.
#   - `reason` must not be empty
column2: and must say why no baseline confronts the rule — not that none does.

column1: #   - `resolved_when` must not be empty. A hole with no written way out is one nobody closes.
#   - A row for a rule that a baseline confronts after all is a failure
# This file is not a way to quiet a rule. A row says "this gate is not measuring this rule"
# worse position than a rule that fails it — the fix is a baseline holding the shape the rule reads
# and a row exists only while that fixture does not.

column2: No baseline carries a Security channel. `baseline-elevated-win11` vendors one .evtx file, a LanguagePackSetup operational log, whose records agree with none of this rule's three conditions. Fabricating a Security log to give the gate something to measure is what fixtures/hosts/PROVENANCE.md forbids: a baseline is the claim that a machine like this is unremarkable, and an invented one claims nothing.
column3: An ordinary Security.evtx captured from a real Windows 11 machine is added to a baseline, with its PROVENANCE row. A real Security log is expected to hold Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog records on the Security channel that are not 1102 — 1100 is written when the Event Log service stops — which would confront this rule at two conditions of three without any clearing having happened. That expectation is unverified and has to be checked against an actual log.
